newsitem.title: USA: Intraday CSCE world sugar weaker as funds sell.
newsitem.headline: Intraday CSCE world sugar weaker as funds sell.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were trading weaker at midsession, pressured by brisk fund selling in the wake of Tuesday's sharp gains, floor sources said.

The previous close sharply off the contract highs set the market up for losses today. Fund selling emerged on the open and pressured the benchmark October contract to the day's low of 11.10 cents, where traders have pegged support.
The next downside target was seen at 11.00 cents, followed by the contract low of 10.96 cents, in October.
At midday, trade buying supported the market just over the days lows while the locals, who went short early, began buying back contracts, dealers said.
While prices are expected to hold current levels through today's session, the increasing liquidity in October could weigh on the market in the near term, analysts said.

As of early Tuesday, open interest in the most-active month rose 3,573 lots to 98,363 lots. Open interest in second-position March, where brisk buying was cited on Tuesday, rose by 1,571 lots to 41,475 lots.
At 1120 EDT, the October contract stood 0.12 cent weaker at 11.12 cents per lb, traded 11.26 to 11.10 cents. The rest of the board was trading down 0.05 to 0.11 cent.
Resistance in October was pegged at its lifetime high of 11.40 cents, followed by 11.50 cents.
An estimated 13,433 lots changed hands as of 1100 EDT.
